attributes.title: Level 6

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓Did you check the Documentation for help with coding the functions needed for the Player sprite?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What do you notice about each of the Player image assets?

❓ What do you think the theme of the sprite pack might be, based on the Player image, Collectible image, tile, and tilemap assets?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to use the documentation if they need help placing the Player sprite on screen or coding its movement.

💡 Prompt the ninja to open each Player image asset. Have them notice the similarities and differences between each image and how they show a different perspective, based on the direction they’re facing.
steps.instructions:
Set up and explore the project’s theme!


Open the Assets menu and notice the 4 Player sprite image assets, each facing a different direction, as well as Collectible sprite, tilemap, and floorTile assets. 


Return to the JavaScript editor, then add a // project start comment. Below, display the tilemap from the Assets menu.


Then, add a // Player sprite code comment and create a Player sprite using the forward facing Player sprite asset. Code the Player sprite to appear on a specific tile, move with the direction buttons, and to stay in screen. Make sure the camera follows the sprite across the tilemap, too.


Click ▶ to see the Player sprite and tilemap appear on screen.

steps.hints: ❓Did you add on button pressed events for left, right, up, and down buttons so that the sprite image updates to the correct image when the direction buttons are pressed?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What might the spriteDirection variable be used for in this project?

❓ Which image asset should be used in each controller event? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that using a variable can be useful for keeping track of game conditions in a project. In a later step, the ninja will add a Projectile sprite. The Projectile sprite will change its direction, based on the direction that the Player sprite is facing.

💡 Make sure the ninja has double checked that the image asset and variable assignment matches the direction in each controller event. Prompt them to test out the project by pressing the direction buttons and checking to see if the sprite’s image updates correctly. They could also add a sayText function to each event to make sure the variable matches the direction of the button pressed.

💡 Encourage the ninja to use documentation if they need help coding the setImage or controller events.
steps.instructions:
Match the Player sprite’s image to the direction it’s facing. 


Under // Player sprite code, declare a spriteDirection variable, set to “down”.


Add a // project events comment, then code the Player sprite’s image to change on left, right, up, and down button pressed events.


Inside each button pressed event, use a string to set the spriteDirection variable to match the direction being pressed. For example, use the string “left” when the left button is pressed.


Click ▶ to see the sprite image update based on the direction button being pressed.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the documentation for help with creating and exporting a new sprite kind from the SpriteKind namespace?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How many Collectible sprites will appear on screen when the project starts?

❓ How does the Collectible sprite fit within the theme of the project? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that a while loop runs while a condition is true. In this example, while there are fewer than 2 Collectible sprites, the placeCollectible function will be called to continue creating Collectible sprites. The loop will stop running once there are 2 Collectible sprites on screen.

💡 Prompt the ninja to think about what other sprites might be added to the project that will pair well with the Player, Collectible, tile, and tilemap assets.

💡 Encourage the ninja to use documentation if they need help creating a new sprite kind or checking the length of an array.
steps.instructions:
Add the Collectible sprite to the project!


Add a // project initialization comment to the top of the editor. Underneath, declare a Collectible sprite kind to be used in the project.


Add a // Collectible sprite code comment, then define a placeCollectible function. Inside the function definition, add code to create a new sprite using the collectible image asset and sprite kind. Then, place the sprite on a random floorTile. 


Use an onUpdate loop with a while loop nested inside to call the placeCollectible function while the length of the array of Collectible sprites is less than 2.


Click ▶ to see multiple Collectible sprites appear on screen.

steps.hints: ❓Did you create a Goal sprite that fits the theme of the project?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What type of image might you create for the Goal  sprite that fits with the theme of the project? 

❓ What colors might be used to create the Goal sprite image?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that in the project, the Player sprite will retrieve the Collectible sprites, and bring them to the Goal sprite. As a result, the Goal image should reflect something that the Player sprite would bring the Collectible sprite (koala) to. 

💡 Have the ninja notice what colors are used in the existing assets to think through the project’s color palette. Prompt the ninja to incorporate some of the same colors, or introduce 1-2 new ones in the Goal sprite image.
steps.instructions:
Create a Goal sprite image that fits the theme of the project!


Consider what type of Goal sprite would fit in with the project theme established by the Player and Collectible sprites.


Create a new image asset to be used as a Goal sprite, one that the Player sprite will bring a Collectible sprite to.


Begin by drawing an outline of the image, then use the erase tool to remove any jaggies from the outline. Add a base color to the image, then add additional features such as highlights and shadows if applicable.

steps.hints: ❓Did you update the run condition in the for loop to place at least 5 Goal sprites on screen?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How many Goal sprites might be placed on the tilemap?

❓ How can a new sprite kind be added to the project?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that the project should be challenging, but not impossible. They should consider this while updating the run condition in the for loop to place the Goal sprites.

💡 Encourage the ninja to use documentation if they need help creating a new sprite kind or placing the Goal sprites.
steps.instructions:
Add the Goal sprite to the project! 


Return to the JavaScript editor, then declare a Goal sprite kind under // project initialization.


Add a // Goal sprite code comment, then use a for loop to create at least 5 Goal sprites using the Goal image asset and sprite kind. Place each sprite on a random floorTile.


Click ▶ to see the Goal sprites appear on screen.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use sprite and otherSprite inside the 2 onOverlap events so the functions will apply to any sprites of that sprite kind?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What will happen when the Player sprite overlaps a Collectible sprite? 

❓ What will happen when a Collectible sprite overlaps a Goal sprite? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the Player sprite overlaps a Collectible sprite, the Collectible sprite should follow the Player sprite so that it can bring it to a Goal sprite.

💡 When a Collectible sprite overlaps a Goal sprite, the Collectible sprite will be destroyed and the score will increase by 1.
steps.instructions:
Make something happen when the Collectible sprite overlaps with a Player or Goal sprite! 


Under // Collectible sprite code, create two onOverlap events, one between the Player and Collectible and one between the Goal and the Collectible.


Use these events to make the Collectible sprite follow the Player sprite after they overlap, then destroy the Collectible sprite after it overlaps a Goal sprite.


Under // project initialization, set the score variable to 0. Then, set the score to increase by 1 when the Collectible sprite overlaps a Goal sprite.


Click ▶ to see the Player sprite “pick up” the Collectible sprite and take it to the Goal sprite.

steps.hints: ❓Did you create an Enemy sprite that fits the theme of the project?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What type of image might you create for the Enemy sprite that fits with the theme of the project? 

❓ What colors might be used to create the Enemy sprite image?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that an Enemy sprite can be a sprite that shows a living thing or an inanimate object. Prompt the ninja to consider what might be a good image for an Enemy sprite, given the theme of the project.

💡 Have the ninja notice what colors are used in the existing assets to think through the project’s color palette. Prompt the ninja to incorporate some of the same colors, or introduce 1-2 new ones in the Enemy sprite image.
steps.instructions:
Create an Enemy sprite image that fits the theme of the project!


Consider what type of Enemy sprite would fit in with the project theme established by the Player, Collectible, and Goal sprites.


Create a new image asset to be used as an Enemy sprite, one that might harm the Player sprite  unless it is hit by a Projectile, which will be created in a later step.


Begin by drawing an outline of the image, then use the erase tool to remove any jaggies from the outline. Add a base color to the image, then add additional features such as highlights and shadows if applicable.

steps.hints: ❓Did you update how frequently Enemy sprites appear in the project, so that is is challenging but not impossible for the user?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How frequently might Enemy sprites appear on the tilemap?

❓ What effect might be used to make the Enemy sprites stand out?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that the project should be challenging, but not impossible. They should consider this while updating the interval parameter in the onUpdateInterval loop to place the Enemy sprites.
steps.instructions:
Add the Enemy sprite to the project! 


Add an // Enemy sprite code comment, then use an onUpdateInterval loop to create Enemy sprites using the Enemy image asset and sprite kind. Add a sprite effect so that the Enemy sprites stand out on the tilemap. Place each sprite on a random floorTile.


Click ▶ to see Enemy sprites appear periodically on the screen. Adjust the interval of the onUpdateInterval loop to make Enemy sprites appear more or less often.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the vertical and horizontal flip tools to create 4 Projectile sprite images?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What type of image might you create for the Projectile sprite? What size canvas might you use?

❓ How might you edit the Projectile sprite images to create assets showing all 4 directions?

 

Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to think through the existing assets in the project and consider what kind of image might be used for the Projectile sprite. Point out that the Projectile sprite will be used to destroy the Enemy sprite and should match accordingly.

💡 It might be useful for the ninja to explore premade Projectile sprite images in MakeCode’s library. Have the ninja notice that Projectiles are often smaller images, typically 8x8 pixels instead of 16x16. Have the ninja tinker with the size of the Projectile image as they are creating.

💡 Have the ninja reflect on how they created person sprites in all 4 directions. Prompt them to consider what is similar about the up, down, left, and right facing images and what should be changed. Encourage the ninja to use the vertical and horizontal flip tools to create the 4 Projectile sprite images.
steps.instructions:
Create a Projectile sprite that fits the theme of the project!


Consider what type of Projectile sprite would fit in with the project theme established by the Player, Enemy, Goal, and Collectible sprites.


Create a new image asset to be used as a Projectile sprite, one that the Player sprite will use to destroy an Enemy sprite. Consider using a smaller 8x8 canvas for the Projectile sprite.


Duplicate the Projectile asset to create a Projectile that faces all 4 possible directions. Use the horizontal and vertical flip tools in the paint editor to change the image direction, then rename the asset appropriately so it can be easily used in the code.

steps.hints: ❓Did you create 4 possible direction conditions inside the createProjectile function and match the Projectile image and velocities accordingly?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What will happen when the A button is pressed?

❓ What should the vx and vy parameters be set to in each of the createProjectileFromSprite functions, so that it moves in the correct direction?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the A button is pressed, a Projectile will be sent from the Player sprite. The Projectile’s image and velocity will match the direction that the Player sprite is facing.

💡 Remind the ninja that the vx parameter sets the speed at which the sprite moves horizontally and the vy parameter sets the speed at which the sprite moves vertically. Positive vx and vy values cause the sprite to move right or down on screen. Negative vx and vy values cause the sprite to move left or up on screen.
steps.instructions:
Add Projectiles to the project!


Add a // Projectile sprite code comment, then underneath, define a createProjectile function with a direction string parameter. 


The spriteDirection variable will be passed to the function as an argument. Use a conditional inside the function that checks for all four direction arguments, then creates a Projectile from the Player sprite set to the matching image asset using the correct vx and vy values so the Projectile moves in the direction expected.


Call the createProjectile function whenever the A button is pressed, passing the spriteDirection variable as the string argument.


Click ▶ then press A to see the Player sprite launch Projectile sprites in all 4 directions!

steps.hints: ❓Did you use sprite and otherSprite inside the 2 onOverlap events so the functions will apply to any sprites of that sprite kind?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What will happen when the Player sprite overlaps an Enemy sprite? 

❓ What will happen when a Collectible sprite overlaps an Enemy sprite? 

❓ What will happen when a Projectile sprite overlaps an Enemy sprite? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡When the Player sprite overlaps an Enemy sprite, the Enemy sprite will be destroyed and the Player will lose a life.

💡When a Collectible or Projectile sprite overlaps an Enemy sprite, both sprites will be destroyed.
steps.instructions:
Make something happen when the Enemy sprite overlaps with Player, Goal, or Projectile sprites! 


Under // Enemy sprite code, create 3 onOverlap events, each between the Enemy sprite and either the Player, Goal, or Projectile sprites.


Use these events to make the Enemy sprite destroy a Goal sprite when they overlap, then to destroy both the Projectile and Enemy sprites when they overlap.


Under // project initialization, set the life variable to 3. Then, decrease the life variable by 1 when the Enemy sprite overlaps the Player sprite, and destroy the Enemy sprite.


Click ▶ to see the Player sprite’s lives decrease on overlap with the Enemy sprite.

steps.hints: ❓Did you select or create image assets for the dialog frame and cursor?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What frame and cursor images might be used to introduce the user to the project theme?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to use what they’ve learned about pixel art, or an existing asset from the project, to create or select frame and cursor images to begin the project.
steps.instructions:
Add instructions to the beginning of the project!


Below // project start, set the dialog frame and dialog cursor image. Use a dialog box to share instructions for the project with the user.


Click ▶ to play the completed project!

subgroups.introduction: Design a sprite pack of assets for a project, using a unifying theme for all of the different sprite kinds in the project.

validationItems.text: Create a Player sprite that changes images when the direction buttons are pressed. Store the sprite’s direction in a spriteDirection variable each time a direction button is pressed.
Use a placeCollectible function to create Collectible sprites. Call the function in an onUpdate loop while there are less than 2 Collectible sprites on screen.
Create Goal, Enemy, and 4 Projectile sprites with unique image assets that fit the theme of the sprite pack.
Use a createProjectile function to create Projectile sprites that move in the direction the Player sprite is facing. Call the function in a button press event.
Use multiple overlap events to make things happen when different sprite kinds from the sprite pack interact.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 6 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about creating images that show multiple perspectives of the same sprite and themed sprite packs for projects. You’ll be able to take the strategies you learn in this level to create detailed assets in future projects! Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 6:

badges.title: Package Deal
badges.description: Create a sprite pack that includes different sprite kinds and different perspectives of those sprites, to be used in a project.

badges.title: Covering All My Bases
badges.description: Create pixel art images that show multiple points of view for a sprite: forward, backward, left, and right.

badges.title: Group by Theme
badges.description: Use a specific color palette and theme to create a sprite pack of different sprite kinds.

badges.title: The Gang’s All Here!
badges.description: Create a sprite pack of original pixel art images that includes Player, Collectible, Goal, Enemy, and Projectile sprites.
